items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: I think the first one was with Roger Wolfe Kahn. Now, as you know, Roger Wolfe Kahn's father was the famous financier, Otto Kahn... I was only with him about six months

ctx.x: So all right, you are going to be leaving Chicago now. Now, let's stick with your career and digress just a little bit perhaps with Bix and Jack as we talk and Pee Wee.
Yes, we got the telegram from Mezzrow. I mentioned this earlier. It was forming this black/white band, and of course, we wanted to be in it.

So, Floyd O'Brien and I got on a bus, you know, the trombone player, and came to join Mezzrow. And we stayed, he had a house up in the Bronx, or up near -- yes, the Bronx, I was going to say near Harlem, but it was way up 167th Street, I think, and he had this big apartment where we stayed, we had no money or anything and we were just rehearsing, and Mezzrow was feeding us and what not, and as I say, the thing didn't take, I mean, with all the help of people like Benny Carter and Alex and what not, the thing…
